newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Lonrho up on JCI merger report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Lonrho up on JCI merger report.

text.p: South African listed shares in mining to hotels group, Lonrho Plc, jumped over two percent shortly after trade started on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday on reports it is to merge with mining house JCI Ltd
Lonrho jumped to an early high of 10.20 rand before coming off to 10.05 rand, a gain of seven cents by 0750 GMT in volume of 2,900 shares.
Lonrho on Monday confirmed that it had had preliminary talks with JCI, but said that it had not considered terms for any combination with the South African mining firm.

However, analysts and dealers in Johannesburg said stocks in JCI and fellow mining house Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, which retains a substantial stake in JCI, had fallen in early trade amid uncertainty about the proposed deal.
"The real issue at the moment is the uncertainty about 4he price at which (Lonrho) will issue the paper," said John Clemmow, an analyst at Investec Securities Ltd.

He said there were a number of ways Lonrho could buy into JCI, including taking the South African firm at its current share price. Lonrho could also issue paper at its current net asset value to fund the purchase.
Dealers said at its current share price Lonrho was a "sound buy", with JCI only a "possible" buy.
JCI shares tumbled 40 cents to 42.40 rand in volume of over 130,000. Anglo was off 225 cents to 268 rand.
Speculation follows a report in a UK newspaper on Sunday that Lonrho is to bid for JCI, which it valued at 900 million sterling, to create one of the world's biggest mining companies.
The newspaper said that Lonrho chairman Sir John Craven had received "imaginative proposals" from JCI, the world's sixth largest gold producer.
